channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: US Congress Approves 'Hell Sanctions' Against Russia, Awaiting President's Signature
item.description: The US Congress has definitively passed a bill imposing 'hell sanctions' on Russia for the war in Ukraine and sent it to President Donald Trump for signing. Experts suggest Trump may delay implementation for four key reasons.

item.title: UN Resident Coordinator in Kyrgyzstan Concludes Mission, Receives Government Commendation
item.description: Antje Grave, the UN Resident Coordinator in Kyrgyzstan, met with Adylbek Kasymaliev upon concluding her mission. They discussed cooperation between Kyrgyzstan and the UN, with Kasymaliev presenting Grave with a certificate of honor for her contributions to strengthening partnership.

item.title: Central Asian Civil Society Forum Discusses Democratic Development in Samarkand
item.description: A forum on the role of civil society institutions in democratic development is underway in Samarkand, featuring around 200 specialists from Central Asia and international experts. Discussions focus on Uzbekistan's and the region's experiences, challenges, and future directions in democratization.

item.title: US Sentences Afghan Militant Linked to Crocus City Hall Attack
item.description: A US court has sentenced an Afghan militant, Mohammad Sharifulah, to 20 years in prison for involvement in terrorist attacks, including providing instructions to the perpetrators of the March 2024 Crocus City Hall attack. The US Justice Department stated he was a key link in ISIS-Khorasan operations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes New Rules for Telecom Operator Licensing
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Digital Development proposes separating telecom operator licensing and radio frequency spectrum allocation. The new rules aim to simplify procedures, ensure transparency, and create equal conditions for participants, with frequencies to be distributed via tender or online auction.

item.title: Tajikistan parliament discusses withdrawal from International Criminal Court
item.description: Tajikistan's lower house parliament discussed a draft resolution on terminating the Rome Statute's effect. The press service confirmed that relevant decisions were made, but details were not provided. Tajikistan is a state party to the ICC, having signed and ratified the Rome Statute in 1998 and 2000 respectively.

item.title: Pashinyan: Armenia will not threaten to leave CSTO, Russian base decision is Moscow's
item.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated that Armenia will not issue threats regarding leaving the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO). He also commented on the Russian military base in Armenia, saying the decision to keep it or withdraw it rests with Moscow. He indicated no need for threats in this regard.

item.title: Chinese Defense Minister Calls for Joint Efforts to Safeguard Peace and Stability
item.description: China's Defense Minister Dong Jun stated that the PLA is ready to work with all parties to protect international and regional stability, create a favorable security environment, and ensure peaceful development. He made these remarks during meetings with defense ministers from Thailand, Mongolia, Cambodia, and Singapore at the Xiangshan Forum in Beijing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ministry to Develop 300 Preschool Education Materials by 2029
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Education will develop 300 innovative, competency-based materials for preschool education by 2029. These materials, for children aged 1-6, educators, and parents, will be available in print, digital, audio, and video formats to foster practical skills development.

item.title: Uzbekistan offers preferential loans up to $5 million for electrical engineering firms
item.description: Uzbekistan will provide preferential loans of up to $5 million to electrical engineering companies. The loans will have a term of up to two years with a three-month grace period and an annual interest rate of 6%. Anchor investors will be exempt from property and profit taxes for 10 years.

item.title: National Security Committee Exposes Misconduct by Naryn Oblast Officials
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security has uncovered financial irregularities in pasture land fee collection by local government officials in Naryn Oblast. Funds collected from residents were not fully remitted to the local budget, causing over 36 million som loss.

item.title: Azerbaijan Pressured France to Lift Sanctions on Alisher Usmanov, Diplomats Claim
item.description: European diplomats allege that Azerbaijan exerted pressure on France to lift sanctions against Russian billionaire Alisher Usmanov. This pressure reportedly came in connection with Azerbaijan's efforts to secure the release of two French citizens detained in the country.

item.title: US Federal Reserve Raises Key Interest Rate for First Time in Three Years
item.description: The US Federal Reserve increased its key interest rate to 3.75-4 percent, the first hike in three years, aiming to combat high inflation. The Fed anticipates further increases this year and next, with a goal to reach 2 percent inflation by 2029.

item.title: Kushoniyon District Sees Major Upgrades for Early Childhood Development
item.description: Kushoniyon District has renovated health and educational facilities and established new early childhood development centers as part of the 'Early Childhood Development for Human Capital Growth in Tajikistan' project. Six primary healthcare facilities were repaired, one new health center built, and a modern preschool prototype created.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Dollar Exchange Rate Rises for Third Consecutive Day
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has increased for the third consecutive day. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan announced the exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective September 18. The announcement details the new values for various foreign currencies.

item.title: Tajikistan and Belarus anti-corruption agencies sign cooperation program
item.description: Tajikistan's Agency for Financial Control and Anti-Corruption and Belarus's Prosecutor General's Office signed a cooperation program for 2027-2028. The agreement aims to strengthen bilateral ties in combating corruption, exchanging information, and conducting joint activities.

item.title: President Sadyr Japarov visits Kyrgyzstan's newly acquired embassy building in Seoul
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov visited Kyrgyzstan's Embassy in Seoul, located in a newly acquired building. He was briefed on the mission's work and noted that the owned premises reduce costs and improve service delivery. The embassy was upgraded from a consulate in 2008.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Minister Pitches Investment Potential to South Korea
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Economy and Commerce, Bakyt Sadykov, presented investment opportunities at the Central Asia-Korea Business Summit. He highlighted the Tamchy Special Financial and Investment Territory, English law operations, and positive GDP growth of 11.1% in 2025 and 11.9% in H1 2026. Trade turnover with South Korea reached $4 billion in 2025.

item.title: Violations Found in State Procurement Exceeding 25 Billion Som in Jizzakh, Sirdaryo, and Fergana Regions
item.description: Violations exceeding 25 billion Uzbekistani som have been identified in state procurement processes in the Jizzakh, Sirdaryo, and Fergana regions. These irregularities were recorded in procurements related to healthcare, education, energy, landscaping, and road construction sectors.

item.title: Uzbekistan Lawmaker Calls for Focus Beyond New Buildings in Education Quality Debate
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber deputy Dilnoza Azizova questioned the impact of increased education budget allocations on teaching quality and teacher standards. While acknowledging the priority given to education through new constructions, she stressed the need to focus on pedagogical competence and teacher-student relationships.

item.title: Uzbekistan condemns drone attack on Mecca, urges restraint
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemned the drone attack on Mecca. The ministry called on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, adhere to international law, and respect the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of states.

item.title: Uzbekistan condemns drone attack attempt on Mecca
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemns the attempted drone attack targeting the holy city of Mecca in Saudi Arabia. The ministry expressed full solidarity with Saudi Arabia, deeming any actions threatening holy sites, civilians, or infrastructure unacceptable. Uzbekistan supports efforts to de-escalate tensions and promote regional peace and security.

item.title: Uzbekistan explains proposed pension system reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Economy and Finance has commented on a draft presidential decree proposing pension reforms. The current system, established in 1993, faces issues including pension calculation based on only the last five years of salary and an outdated income ceiling. Reforms aim to address these challenges and improve the system's sustainability.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Belarus Prepare for Inter-Parliamentary Forum in Khiva
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate hosted a meeting to prepare for the Uzbekistan-Belarus inter-parliamentary forum scheduled for September 29-30 in Khiva. The forum aims to strengthen strategic partnership through parliamentary dialogue and improve the legal framework for trade and economic cooperation, building on recent high-level agreements.

item.title: Tajikistan-Korea Strategic Investment Forum Held in Seoul
item.description: A Tajikistan-Korea Strategic Investment Forum took place in Seoul on September 17, 2026, during President Emomali Rahmon's official visit to South Korea. Over 250 participants, including 200 Korean entrepreneurs and investors, attended. Agreements were signed to strengthen economic and investment ties between the two countries.

item.title: Tajikistan Outlines Transport Priorities at Seoul Conference
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Transport, Azim Ibrohim, presented the country's transport infrastructure and international connectivity priorities at the GICC 2026 conference in Seoul. He emphasized the importance of modern, reliable transport for socio-economic development and trade, highlighting Tajikistan's readiness to expand cooperation with international partners and investors.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presents Critical Minerals Development Strategy in Seoul
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Natural Resources, Akyl Toktobaev, presented the country's critical minerals development strategy at the Korea-Central Asia Business Summit in Seoul. He highlighted Kyrgyzstan's resource potential, the need to diversify mining, and invited international cooperation for projects from exploration to processing.

item.title: First Phase of Bishkek Solar Power Plant Launched in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The first phase of the 100-megawatt Bishkek Solar power plant has been launched in Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul region. Implemented with Russian specialists, the project was inaugurated remotely by President Sadyr Japarov. This launch exemplifies successful Russia-Kyrgyz cooperation in the energy sector.

item.title: UN report: Large-scale war identified as top global risk
item.description: A new UN report, based on a survey of experts, identifies large-scale war as the most acute global risk. It has risen 16 positions since 2024, with 36% expecting consequences within a year. The international community is least prepared for this threat.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Banks See Deposits Fall by 24.5 Billion Soms in July
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's banking sector experienced a significant outflow of deposits totaling 24.5 billion soms in July 2026, according to the National Bank. Despite this decline, total bank assets also decreased by 6.4 percent over the month. Concurrently, loan issuance reached record highs.

item.title: Printing house banned from selling textbooks to private schools
item.description: The Ministry of Education has prohibited the "Uchkun" printing house from selling textbooks to private educational institutions. The ministry will now collect information from private schools to determine textbook orders. Previously, the printing house sold books without restrictions, as it lacked the right to verify buyers.

item.title: State document production: "Uchkun" OJSC implements triple security control
item.description: The "Uchkun" printing house, a subsidiary of the Kyrgyz president's administration, employs triple security control for state document production. This includes МВД (Ministry of Internal Affairs) security, internal security, and national security organs. Advanced scanning equipment and video surveillance are used in sensitive areas.

item.title: Tajikistan cotton harvest reaches 39,200 tons
item.description: As of September 14, farmers in Tajikistan have harvested 39,190 tons of cotton. Approximately 70,000 pickers are involved in the harvest. Cotton production is a strategic sector for Tajikistan, with a goal of over 394,000 tons by 2026.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host CIS Digitalization and Communications Development Forum
item.description: Dushanbe will host joint meetings of the CIS Communications Administrations Heads Council, CIS Informatization Coordination Council, and ITU Regional Forum on Development for the CIS region from September 29-30, 2026. Discussions will focus on telecommunications, digitalization, cybersecurity, and regional cooperation.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Meets with South Korean National Assembly Speaker
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon met with South Korean National Assembly Speaker Cho Jung-sik in Seoul. They discussed strengthening inter-parliamentary dialogue, economic cooperation, investment, and joint projects, emphasizing the importance of regional stability and development initiatives.

item.title: US Federal Reserve Hikes Interest Rate for First Time in Over Three Years
item.description: The US Federal Reserve raised its key interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.75-4%, the first increase since July 2023. Fed Chair Jerome Powell cited persistently high inflation as the reason, noting that underlying inflation trends have not significantly improved. The decision comes amid ongoing cost-of-living pressures for American households.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Mechanisms to Support Electrotechnical Industry
item.description: Uzbekistan has established new mechanisms to finance working capital, purchase copper raw materials, and attract foreign investors for its electrotechnical industry. Loans of up to $5 million will be available at a 6% annual interest rate with a two-year term, starting October 1, 2026.

item.title: Trump to Discuss Iran Strategy with Gulf Leaders at UN General Assembly
item.description: US President Donald Trump plans to meet with leaders of Persian Gulf countries at the UN General Assembly in New York. The primary topic will be future strategy concerning Iran. The meeting is expected to focus on next steps following the conflict with Tehran, with a plan possibly approved after US midterm elections.

item.title: Trump threatens EU trade halt over Canada rapprochement
item.description: US President Donald Trump criticized the European Commission's proposal to make Canada an associate member of the EU, calling it "ridiculous." He threatened to impose heavy tariffs or completely halt trade with Europe if this move is considered hostile. The European Commission had proposed closer ties with Canada.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Sign 15 Cooperation Documents
item.description: Tajikistan and South Korea signed 15 new cooperation documents in Seoul on September 16, 2026. Agreements cover customs, intellectual property, education, economy, anti-corruption, financial intelligence, industry, transport, forest restoration, export, labor safety, energy, public service, and law enforcement cooperation.
